sections.h2: Which Union County offices touch a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Union County keeps its tax work in Morganfield, and the PVA and the sheriff both list 100 West Main Street. The PVA describes itself as a state office with county jurisdiction, charged with valuing property as of January 1. It says plainly that it does not set rates, work out the tax or collect it.

  • PVA: PO Box 177, Morganfield, KY 42437. Phone (270) 389-1933, open weekdays 8:00 to 4:00. This is where exemptions are filed.
  • Sheriff, the payee: PO Box 30, Morganfield, KY 42437. Phone (270) 389-1303, with the same weekday hours.
  • County Clerk, who records deeds and later holds unpaid bills: (270) 389-1334.

The county government site adds a tax roll search, a tax calculator and a rate page under the PVA menu, handy for checking a parcel before you call.

sections.h2: What sets Union County apart for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Union sits in the far northwest corner of Kentucky, on the east bank of the Ohio where the Wabash joins it. The county was created effective January 15, 1811, and together with Posey County, Indiana and Gallatin County, Illinois it marks the point where three states meet. Low wooded hills break up flat farmland, and the high point, 673 feet, is in the Chalybeate Hills inside the Higginson-Henry Wildlife Management Area. The county belongs to the Western Coal Fields region.

Four cities share the county: Morganfield, the seat and largest, plus Sturgis, Uniontown and Waverly. US 60, KY 56 and KY 109 carry the traffic, and the John T. Myers Locks and Dam, opened in 1977, stands 3.5 miles below Uniontown. Union County Public Schools runs elementary schools in Morganfield, Sturgis and Uniontown, one middle school and Union County High School, and the public library has branches in the same three towns.

Union has been losing people for decades. The 1900 census counted 21,326, and the 2020 count was 13,668. The July 2025 estimate is 12,839.

With no permits recorded in 2025, nearly every sale is a resale, so buyers price in the condition of a house and the state of its tax account. Employer businesses numbered 249 in 2023, with 3,980 jobs and payroll near $228 million, and employment grew 8.2 percent that year. About 52.5 percent of people 16 or older are in the labor force.

sections.h2: What does the state rate add up to on a Union County house?
sections.html:
The Commonwealth levies 10.6 cents per hundred dollars of assessed value for 2025, a small drop from 10.9 cents. At the $104,500 median home value that is $110.77. County, school and other districts bring the full bill well above it.

The $49,100 homestead deduction brings the taxable base on that house to $55,400 and the state portion to about $58.72. Union County has 21.9 percent of its residents at 65 or older, and 23.1 percent of residents under 65 report a disability, so the deduction speaks to many households here. Apply at the PVA on West Main. Disability claims renew annually, except for service connected veterans and for owners ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What is the Union County payment calendar?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 sets one schedule for all counties. Union's sheriff discounts a bill by 2 percent through November 1, accepts the printed amount through December, and then adds 5 percent in January and 10 percent after that, plus an additional sheriff's fee.

Each April 15 the sheriff's delinquent listings pass to the County Clerk, with a lien recorded. The clerk's page says a county sale of those bills is usually held in September of the year following the tax year and is posted online about a month beforehand. Anyone who wants to bid registers with the clerk first, and the state also requires registration for a buyer taking more than three certificates in this county, more than five statewide, or putting in more than $10,000.

sections.h2: What does a late Union County bill grow into?
sections.html:
The Department of Revenue shows the growth on a model $1,000 bill. After the 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's add on and an assumed 4 percent commission it stands at $1,254.00 on reaching the clerk. Interest of 1 percent a month then runs, and commissions follow the interest.

  • With the attorney's first letter sent: $1,611.30.
  • If settled in May: $1,627.61.
  • If settled in June after advertising: $1,659.90.
  • If a third party buys it at the sale: $1,704.21, before that buyer's own charges.

The lien lasts up to 11 years under KRS 134.420 and passes with the land to any new owner. A Union County seller with arrears should get a payoff figure from the clerk and have the title company pay it at closing.

sections.h2: How does a Union County owner dispute an assessment?
sections.html:
Meet with the PVA before filing anything, since the state refuses appeals that skip that conversation. The roll goes on public view for thirteen days from the first Monday in May. Once you have met, bring the appeal to the clerk by the end of the day after the viewing period closes.

The local board of assessment appeals hears cases between 25 and 35 days later and sits as long as five days. It denies an appeal that lacks factual support, so collect sale comparisons, repair bids and photos. An owner who neither files nor shows up cannot go further to the Kentucky Claims Commission. A written explanation follows any change, you may record the hearing, and a higher final value brings a supplemental bill.

sections.h2: How are deeds and records handled by the Union County Clerk?
sections.html:
The clerk's office at 100 West Main Street holds recorded land documents going back to 1811, mostly deeds, mortgages, assignments and releases. Kentucky wants a deed lodged in the county where the land lies, citing the seller's source of title, and KRS 382.135 adds mailing addresses, the full price, an in care of address for that year's bill and a sworn certificate of price.

The clerk offers e-filing so a title company can send documents without mail or courier. Union County residents can search the records online for personal reasons at no charge, up to five searches a day, and anyone may use the public records in the office for free. Commercial researchers pay $65 a month per county through the records vendor.

For a seller with a tenant, a probate problem or a house that needs repairs, a cash purchase as is avoids waiting on a retail buyer's inspection.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Union County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay the sheriff at 100 West Main Street in Morganfield, or mail to PO Box 30. The phone number is (270) 389-1303 and the office keeps weekday hours from 8:00 to 4:00.

faqs.q: Does the Union County PVA send my bill?
faqs.a: No. The PVA values property and handles exemptions, but the county's own page says it does not set rates, calculate taxes or collect them. The sheriff handles billing and payment.

faqs.q: When is the Union County delinquent tax sale?
faqs.a: It is usually held in September of the year after the tax year. The County Clerk posts the exact date on the county website about a month ahead, at (270) 389-1334 for questions.

faqs.q: Can I look up a Union County parcel online?
faqs.a: Yes. The county government site has a tax roll search and a tax calculator under the PVA pages, plus a rate page, so you can see the owner and assessed value.

faqs.q: What is the typical home value in Union County?
faqs.a: Census QuickFacts lists $104,500 as the median owner occupied value for 2020 to 2024. That is well below the $172,000 in Trimble County and $258,000 in Warren County.
